election._note: By law no later than June 2029 (2024 Assembly's 5-year term); Wikipedia 'Next French legislative election'

dissolution._note: Art. 12: the President may dissolve the Assembly after consulting the PM and the presidents of both chambers, no approval required. Elections must be held 20-40 days later. No second dissolution within a year of the previous one. Lexology, 'The French President announces the dissolution of the National Assembly'; france24.com, 'France's dissolution of parliament, snap elections'.

amendment._note: Art. 89: a revision bill must pass both chambers in identical terms, then either a popular referendum or -- the President's choice, and the only path this game models -- a joint session of both chambers (Congress) at Versailles requiring a 3/5 majority of votes cast. Legifrance, Constitution of 4 October 1958, Title XVI.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: Art. 89 §5: 'The republican form of government shall not be the object of an amendment.' No amendment may change France's system_id at all, not merely at a higher bar.

executive._note: First round 18 April 2027, run-off 2 May 2027; five-year term. This is the PLAYER's term and it is a different clock from the Assembly's -- france24.com 'France sets presidential election date', Wikipedia '2027 French presidential election'.
executive.title: President of the Republic

formation._note: President appoints the Prime Minister; there is no investiture vote. A motion de censure carries only with an absolute majority of the members (289 of 577) -- abstentions and absences count as against. Art. 49 of the 1958 Constitution; connexionfrance.com 'What is a motion de censure'.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. Authored per nation because the law is generic and the dynasty is not; a monarchy points this at its own sitting monarch.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/OECD estimates ~2023-2024, rounded. Starting policy is the V1.2a anchor -- every other nation's tax_rates_pct/spending_pct_gdp/other_spending_pct_gdp is France's, scaled: VAT is each nation's own sourced statutory rate, income and corporate are France's scaled by that nation's OECD Revenue Statistics personal/corporate tax-to-GDP share, and the five spending lines plus other_spending_pct_gdp are France's split scaled by general-government-expenditure-to-GDP. France's own numbers are therefore unchanged from V1.1 and are not derived from anything below.
